domain: Constitutional Law / Legal Pluralism / Comparative Family Law
topic_summary: Analysis of India's coexisting personal-law regimes governing marriage, divorce, inheritance, and family matters under Hindu, Muslim, Christian, Parsi, and secular frameworks within a single constitutional state. The system has persisted for 75+ years without zero-sum resolution, raising the question of whether this represents one contested kernel (marriage/family law authority) read through multiple religious lenses, or genuinely distinct kernels coexisting without unified normative foundation.

key_entities: Hindu Personal Law (codified 1950s: Hindu Marriage Act 1955, Hindu Succession Act 1956, applies to Hindus/Buddhists/Jains/Sikhs)
Muslim Personal Law (Shariat Application Act 1937, largely uncodified, textual interpretation)
Christian Personal Law (Indian Christian Marriage Act 1872, Indian Divorce Act 1869)
Parsi Personal Law (Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act 1936)
Special Marriage Act 1954 (secular civil marriage alternative)
Article 44 (Directive Principle: state shall endeavor to secure uniform civil code)
Supreme Court of India (Shah Bano 1985, Sarla Mudgal 1995, Shayara Bano 2017)
Darul Qaza (Sharia courts, community-based adjudication parallel to state courts)
key_tensions: Legal pluralism vs constitutional equality (Article 44 directive vs community autonomy)
Gender justice asymmetry (differential inheritance/divorce rights across regimes)
Codification asymmetry (Hindu law fully codified vs Muslim law textual/interpretive)
Parallel adjudication (state courts vs community courts with overlapping jurisdiction)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Marriage and family law authority — the state's claim to adjudicate legitimate family formation, dissolution, inheritance, and maintenance
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Contested between constitutional supremacy (Article 44 UCC directive + fundamental rights) and religious community autonomy (personal law as protected minority right)
commitment_system_recognition.kernel_collapse_reason: The five regimes do NOT read one shared kernel differently — they instantiate genuinely distinct kernels with non-overlapping normative foundations. Hindu law grounds authority in codified statutory reform (1950s modernization); Muslim law grounds authority in Sharia textual interpretation (pre-state religious law); Christian/Parsi laws ground authority in colonial-era statutory frameworks; Special Marriage Act grounds authority in secular constitutional citizenship. These are not different readings of 'what marriage law is' — they are different answers to 'what grounds the authority to define marriage at all.' The system is an incoherent bundle, not a contested kernel. No single coherent normative framework could hold all five as complementary readings of one commitment.
commitment_system_recognition.structural_implication: This is D2 culture-level break material: the system tests whether legal pluralism can sustain without unified normative foundation. Decompose into flat axes capturing the structural mechanics of coexistence rather than kernel readings.

omegas.description: The five regimes are NOT readings of one kernel but genuinely distinct kernels with non-overlapping normative foundations (statutory reform vs Sharia text vs colonial statute vs secular citizenship). This is incoherent bundle, not contested kernel. The system tests whether legal pluralism can sustain without unified normative foundation — D2 culture-level break material.

Special Marriage Act 1954 provides secular alternative but usage rate is unknown. If high, reveals preference for exit over voice (pluralism as trap). If low, reveals social cost of secular path (rope becomes snare via community enforcement).

omegas.description: Is Supreme Court convergence (Shah Bano, Shayara Bano) a Scaffold (building toward UCC) or Piton (atrophied legislative capacity)? If judicial path succeeds, legislative UCC becomes unnecessary. If judicial path stalls, gender justice fragmentation persists indefinitely.

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: codification_asymmetry classified as mountain but may be piton of political choice. Hindu law codification in 1950s was deliberate state intervention, not natural law. Muslim law non-codification may reflect community resistance to state penetration rather than inherent textual nature. Generated omega_colonial_continuity to bound this uncertainty. Kernel collapse finding (is_contested_kernel=false) is high-confidence structural judgment but may miss normative coherence invisible to model's training data.
